title: BA1/2659/2023 of KAUSHAL CHILWAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
First Bail Application No.2659 of 2023
Kaushal Chilwal ........Applicant

Present:-
Mr. R.S. Sammal, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. M.A. Khan, AGA for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 Applicant Kaushal Chilwal is in judicial
custody in Case Crime/FIR No.527 of 2022, under
Sections 302 & 34 IPC, Police Station Ramnagar, District
Nainital. He has sought his release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. According to the FIR, the deceased Bhaskar
telephoned his sister-in-law on 04.12.2022 between 8:30-
9:00 PM that he was with his friends. He was in the
residence of his friend co-accused Avdhesh Singh Jeena,
where the applicant and the co-accused were also present
and after a while he would go back to his home. Next
morning, the informant, who happened to be the brother
of the deceased came to know that the deceased has been
killed. He lodged an FIR.

2
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would
submit that it is a false case. The informant himself has
stated that he was given the name of accused by the
police. The wife of informant did not know the applicant
and the co-accused. Therefore, it is argued that it is not
possible that she could collect the name of assailants.
5. Learned State Counsel would submit that the
neighbour Om Prakash of co-accused Avdhesh Singh
Jeena has stated that in the night of incident, the
applicant along with co-accused was in a room of co-accused Avdhesh Singh Jeena. Next morning, the dead
body of the deceased was found from his room.
6. It is the stage of bail. Much of the discussion
at this stage is not expected of. To the extent of
appreciating the controversy, the matter may be examined
with the caveat that any observation, made at this stage,
shall have no bearing at any subsequent stage of the
case.
7. The FIR records that the deceased has
telephonically told his sister-in-law (PW4 Smt. Komal
Pandey) that he is in the room of co-accused Avdhesh
Singh Jeena, where the applicant was also present.

3
8. The Court wanted to know from the learned
State Counsel as to whether the call detail confirms that
the deceased has telephoned his sister-in-law (PW4 Smt.
Komal Pandey) on the date of incident. The reply is in
negative. Learned State Counsel would submit that the
reply is based on instructions.
9. PW1, the informant, has stated that he was
revealed the names of assailants by the police. The
question is that if the wife of informant was not
telephoned on the date of incident, how the names of the
applicant and the co-accused were recorded in the FIR.
10. Having considered, this Court is of the view
that it is a case fit for bail and the applicant deserves to
be enlarged on bail.
11. The bail application is allowed.
12. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his
executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable
sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the
court concerned.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J)
 21.05.2024
Ravi
